observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with white walls, a light wood floor, a dark ceiling with track lighting and an air-conditioning unit, and a full-height mirror covering the right wall. A woman with long dark hair, wearing an embellished teal/green top and a flowing layered blue skirt, stands center-left facing the mirror; the figure seen on the right side of the frame is her mirror reflection, not a second person. The camera viewpoint is fixed throughout (ceiling lights, AC unit and mirror seams hold constant positions).
visible_changes: At the start the dancer's hands are curled close to her face/chest; over the first ~0.4 s she opens her palms and raises them to shoulder/head height, facing the mirror.
From about t=0.48 to t=1.0 s she sweeps both arms out to one side while her torso and hips turn slightly; her long hair swings laterally during this turn, and the skirt shifts with the body.
From about t=1.04 to t=1.3 s she lifts both arms upward until they are fully extended overhead.
From about t=1.3 s to t=1.5 s she brings her hands together above her head to form a closed shape, then at the end of the segment (t=1.56–1.60 s) opens them again overhead.
Her reflection reproduces these same arm and body movements in mirrored form throughout.
The dancer's feet remain roughly planted in place; the visible motion is upper-body and arm choreography plus hair/skirt flow, not locomotion across the floor.
outside_clip_unknowns: The dance phrase continues before t=0 and after t=1.6 s; the segment's endpoints are arbitrary crops and need not form a completed move.
The music, count, or intention behind each gesture is not visible.
Whether the side-sweep involves a step or pivot of the feet is not clearly resolvable from these frames.
uncertain_details: Exact footwork during the side sweep is partly hidden by the skirt and back angle.
The precise hand configuration at the overhead peak (touching vs. near-touching) is small and hard to confirm frame-by-frame.
Minor sway of the skirt may be residual motion rather than a new action.
